title: "His Name Is Lancelot" Spamalot Choreography
abstract: Winter quarter at Northwestern can be a difficult time for students as the harsh weather and rigorous classwork can feel like a heavy weight to bear. For this reason, we were extremely excited to choreography Monty Python’s Spamalot, a musical produced in Winter 2020 by the Northwestern student theatre production board Lovers & Madmen. The production was presented to us as a source of joy and laughter for the students who came to see it during winter quarter. Spamalot, adapted from the film Monty Python and the Holy Grail, spoofs both Arthurian legend and the tropes of the musical theatre canon. In the middle of act two, the number “His Name Is Lancelot” presents King Arthur’s bravest knight, Sir Lancelot, discovering and eventually embracing his sexuality through a disco-infused musical sequence. The number is a celebration of self-acceptance and LGBTQI+ pride, and we highlighted the joy presented in this number through the choreography. By using popular LGBTQI+ dance forms, including waacking and voguing, we created a piece that celebrated LGBTQI+ culture instead of portraying stereotypes that are often presented in the choreography of this number. We fostered an environment of play and creativity while teaching this number so that our dancers could feel supported and proud of the work they were putting into the piece. We challenged our dancers to push themselves out of their comfort zones while still playing to their strengths so that we were able to both teach them new forms of dance while letting them shine with their own individuality and sense of self-acceptance. We are proud to say that the joy and laughter created from this piece helped to lift some of the winter quarter weight from the dancers who performed and the audience members who observed. The performers seen in this video are Nathan Karnik as Lancelot, Clay Lawhead as Prince Herbert, and Jay Towns, Rick Hilscher, Zeke Albro, Alexander Christie, and Jude Cramer as the Dance Ensemble.
